correctness.rationale: For coprime n,m and generators x_i,y^n,y^m,x_i^{lambda_i}y, y is integral and belongs to the same fraction field, so B=C[x_i,y] is the normalization. The semigroup H=<n,m> and q(b)=b-max(H∩[0,b]) give exact monomial membership x^a y^b in R iff u(a)=sum floor(a_i/lambda_i)>=q(b), because all mixed-generator counts 0..u(a) are attainable. Requiring membership of every y^t multiple gives conductor iff u(a)>=Q(b)=max_{t>=b}q(t). Missing monomials per b<c are stars-and-bars binom(q(b)+s-2,s-1) times product lambda_i; for m=n+1 the block gaps sum to binom(n+s-1,s+1). Independent enumerations checked 1341 membership/conductor cases and sample exact deltas. Finite tests do not establish generality.

value.rationale: The precise conductor ideal and finite normalization quotient length are natural invariants of isolated toric singularities, refining actual published bounds and extending across dimension, conductor thresholds and generator multiplicities. The sharp consecutive-semigroup binomial closed form is independently reusable in surface and higher-dimensional examples.

limitations: Only C and the specified minimal-embedding monomial family. Formula is a finite numerical-semigroup sum for arbitrary coprime n,m.
